title: End–to–End Atomic Electron Tomography Reconstruction and Alignment Using Deep Learning Techniques
content: Atomic electron tomography (AET) is a powerful technique for studying nanomaterials, as knowing the precise 3D atomic coordinates allows for first principles studies to better understand their fundamental physical properties. Current methods in performing AET reconstructions rely on analytic and iterative algorithms such as filtered-back projection (FBP), simultaneous iterative reconstruction technique (SIRT) [1], or real-space iterative reconstruction (RESIRE) [2]. However, these techniques are frequently plagued by three issues: the missing wedge problem, noisy data, and imperfect alignment of the dataset. To resolve the first two issues, deep learning techniques have been used to great success in cryo-TEM. Algorithms such as DeepDeWedge [3], IntraTomo [4], and IsoNet [5] leverage techniques such as self-supervised learning and generative inpainting to fill in the sinogram or denoise the resulting tomogram. Despite these advancements, alignment remains a significant bottleneck, as it accounts for the majority of the reconstruction time. Additionally, these deep learning, algebraic, and iterative approaches demand high-quality input data that is time-intensive to preprocess.
